productionArtifactMarkerGate.actual: 222 JavaScript files inspected; no listed text markers found, while mockServiceWorker.js is present as a 9,666-byte public asset.

finding.owner: vite.config.ts build.copyPublicDir and scripts/check-production-mocks.mjs artifact inventory
finding.observedCause: The worker is not pulled into the production source import graph. Vite's enabled default public-directory copy copies public/mockServiceWorker.js byte-for-byte into build output; the marker-only check accepts that worker because it does not assert a forbidden file manifest/path.
finding.risk: Every current production build carries the development MSW service-worker script (9,666 raw bytes; C02.04 recorded 3,226 gzip-9 and 2,718 Brotli-q11 bytes). It can be directly requested and may be registered by an old client; this audit proves presence and copy behavior, not actual registration in production.
finding.acceptanceDirection: Keep public/mockServiceWorker.js available to the Vite development server while proving an isolated production build omits it and all non-production files. Add artifact-level negative checks in C04.03 so a copied worker fails even if its content has no forbidden marker.
finding.rollbackNote: Keep the original public worker source; restore the build-copy setting if a legitimate release asset in public must be shipped, after classifying and explicitly checking it. The existing dist directory must remain preserved during isolated builds.

conclusion: C04.01 source and output audit complete. Fresh C02 isolated build inputs still match current source, but repository dist is older and differs in 205 of 221 chunk paths/content. Both the fresh profile and current dist contain the public worker. Source import gates pass; the current JS-marker gate does not detect this file-level leak.
limits: No source, build configuration, or dist file was changed during this audit.
The current dist was not rebuilt in this step; the C02.04 manifest is an isolated-temp build artifact and was used as an input-matched comparison.
The audit did not run a production deployment, register the worker in a production browser, or verify backend/staging behavior.
